17.epoque: Psalm 90 is attributed to Moses and is set in a context of reflection on the fragility of human life in the face of God's eternity. This psalm is a cry of despair and hope, expressing the necessity of divine grace in a world marked by mortality.
17.passage: This passage is found at the end of the psalm, where the author implores God to bless the work of men. The entire chapter addresses the brevity of life and the importance of living wisely, recognizing our dependence on God.
17.culture: In Hebrew culture, work and human effort were considered essential elements of life, but they were also seen as insufficient without divine intervention. The community valued prayer to seek God's blessing on their efforts.
17.interpretation: This verse reminds us that, although we are called to work and act, our ultimate success depends on God's grace. It teaches us humility and dependence, inviting us to seek divine favor in all our endeavors.
17.commentaire: As believers, we must recognize that our efforts cannot bear lasting fruit without God's blessing. This verse encourages us to pray for the Lord's grace to be upon us, so that our works may be established. By placing our trust in God, we can be assured that our actions, even the most modest, can have an eternal impact.
